text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Reindeer farmers in Lapland are faced with threat of loss of herd as poor weather has destroyed the natural food of the animals.
- Swedish-speaking Finns in the coastal regions enjoy higher standards of living than most other Finns, study shows.
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's Social Democratic Party council supports government's EU policy, calls for ongoing studies of pros and cons of EMU membership. @
- U.S. space agency NASA, has expressed interest in Finnish-made high-tech devices which were among equipment onboard Russian Mars-bound space probe unsuccessfully launched on Saturday.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Pellervo Economic Research Institute (PTT) head of research Mikael Ingberg urges Bank of Finland to allow inflation to rise near two percent core CPI target, noting too tight monetary policy has caused deflation. @
- Finnish pulp producers expect pulp prices to turn higher in 1997 as Norscan pulp inventories are expected to decline in November-December after smaller-than-expected October rise.
- Merrill Lynch raised earnings per share forecasts for Nokia Oy and maintained medium- and long term "buy" recommendation.
- Finnish retailer Rautakirja Oy has investigated possibilities to buy Swedish retail chain Pressbyra from Axel Johnson group. Rautakirja CEO Raimo Hertto denies the report. @

- German magazine Wirtschaftswoche says Finnish sauna equipment maker Oy Saunatec Ltd's net sales expected to rise to 210 million markka by 1998 from 173 million in 1996, and earnings per share to rise to 5.10 markka in 1996 and 7.5 markka in 1998. Saunatec 1995 net sales were 157 million markka, and EPS 4.08 markka. Saunatec CEO Pekka Piisku declines comment.
DEMARI

- It is important that Finland does not remain outside any new European security arrangement, says Bank of Finland director and board of management member, former finance minister and MP Matti Louekoski. @
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen calls for more efforts in Finland to influence the future direction of EMU instead of efforts to oppose the single currency project.
AAMULEHTI

- Navigation in Finnish waters likely to face difficulties if winter becomes harsh because increase in exports has outstripped the capacity of existing ice breakers, board of navigation official says. @
TURUN SANOMAT

- Eighty-nine year old retired police chief ready to donate 700,000 markka to the city of Turku in order to have statue of olympic legend Paavo Nurmi moved to city sport centre from the middle of the city.
--Helsinki Newsroom +358 - 9 - 680 50 292
